significance: A rock-cut cave shrine to Shiva in the Aravalli foothills on the Rajsamand–Pali border, dated to 1005 CE and reached by a climb of some five hundred steps from Sadri. It holds naturally formed figures of Shiva and Ganesha and nine kunds that are said never to run dry.
story: Parashurama, the sixth incarnation of Vishnu, is said to have cut the cave out with his axe and performed severe penance to Shiva here.
